title: One slow command on Redis's main thread makes every other client wait
captions: I/O threads (if you turn them on) read and parse requests. But one main thread runs every command, one after another. A GET takes microseconds, so the queue moves fast.
Someone runs KEYS * on a database with 10 million keys. The main thread must walk every key before it can do anything else.
Clients A, B and C sent tiny GETs. Their requests wait in line, even if I/O threads have already read them. Their timeouts fire, and many clients retry, which adds more load.
The fix: SCAN walks the keys a small batch per call. Other commands run between the batches, so nobody waits long.
